text: The furnished room received its latest guest. <break time="0.8s" /> With a tired, empty sort of welcome. <break time="0.8s" /> Like the forced smile of someone. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had greeted too many strangers. <break time="0.8s" /> A ragged couch and two chairs. <break time="0.8s" /> A cheap mirror between the windows. <break time="0.8s" /> And a brass bed stood about while a bright rug lay like an island. <break time="0.8s" /> On dirty matting. <break time="0.8s" /> On the walls hung the pictures. <break time="0.8s" /> That follow lodgers from house to house. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as The Huguenot Lovers. <break time="0.8s" /> And Psyche at the Fountain. <break time="0.8s" /> In their tired frames. <break time="0.8s" /> One by one as if they were witnesses. <break time="0.8s" /> The marks of earlier tenants appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> A worn spot in the rug. <break time="0.8s" /> And a stain where a thrown bottle had broken. <break time="0.8s" /> Across the mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> Someone had scratched the name Marie with a diamond. <break time="0.8s" /> As if each tenant had wanted. <break time="0.8s" /> To leave some proof. <break time="0.8s" /> Of having once been there. <break time="0.8s" /> The couch had burst its springs. <break time="0.8s" /> And the marble mantel had lost a piece. <break time="0.8s" /> For people seemed to take out their anger. <break time="0.8s" /> On a home that was never truly theirs. <break time="0.8s" /> From the house came a mix of sounds. <break time="0.8s" /> A giggle, a scolding voice. <break time="0.8s" /> The rattle of dice, a lullaby, a banjo. <break time="0.8s" /> And a cat crying on a back fence. <break time="0.8s" /> He breathed the breath of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> A damp and musty smell. <break time="0.8s" /> Like that of a cellar. <break time="0.8s" /> Mixed with the odors. <break time="0.8s" /> Of old linoleum and rotting wood.
